correctness.rationale: For a boundary datum of seminorm L the leaf-imposed center intervals intersect pairwise, hence have a common intersection. A slope-maximizing pair makes this intersection a singleton and forces the center to be its length-weighted interpolant. Absolute minimality forces linearity on every subinterval inside an arm. Conversely, the resulting affine-on-arms function is absolutely minimizing: a connected interior test set within an arm has its slope witnessed by its endpoints; in a test set containing the center, the two saturated arms persist up to the boundary of the center component and witness the global slope. For disconnected sets, splice the path between any two interior points at the boundary of their components. The center selector is continuous and switches only at finitely many comparisons along any line segment (permanent ties give the same center). On each piece, the change of arm i's slope is (h_i-C_ab(h))/ell_i. Its norm is one for i in the selected pair and at most 1+2 ell_a ell_b/((ell_a+ell_b)ell_i) otherwise by the two boundary pair constraints and the barycentric weights. These latter constraints can be saturated together by the proposed perturbation; the base datum has a strict maximizing pair, so a positive finite step preserves the selector and realizes equality. The harmonic mean is increasing in each argument, giving the ordered-length formula including ties. Two arms give a single affine interpolant and ratio one. Constant inputs and ties introduce no singular cases.
residual_risks: Recorded finite checks are corroboration only. The LP code compares the maximum of all selector-coordinate norms to the formula, and rational examples check actual attained ratios; neither is needed for the proof.

originality.rationale: Classical AMLE and weighted graph extensions supply existence, uniqueness or a center rule. The distinct contribution supported by the comparison is the exact Lipschitz-seminorm amplification between two scalar AMLEs on arbitrary positive-length metric stars, with finite attainment. Neither linear harmonic extension on the same metric object nor finite-p energy minimization on unit stars identifies this invariant.

value.rationale: The Lipschitz seminorm of a difference is a quantitative stability question for the canonical AMLE, not answered by its norm-one action on each datum or by sup-norm stability. The result exposes a precise geometric cause of error amplification, identifies the two longest and one shortest arms as the only required lengths, and gives exact extremizers even for equal arms. This is a useful sharp benchmark for stability on trees with more than one branch point, without claiming such a generalization.
residual_risks: Finite scalar stars only; no quantitative claim on general trees or other norms.
